display.purpose: ONIRIA on the home page, stamped.

name.purpose: The character's name written on a printed field line (2rem on phone); team names use the same hand.

page-title.purpose: Tables de jeu, Whitelist: stamped, uppercase.

section.purpose: Section headings, preceded by an armillary sphere and followed by a printed rule; also the title band.

group.purpose: LE CORPS, L’ESPRIT, VUE D’ENSEMBLE: typewriter bold, uppercase.

label.purpose: Field labels (NOM, ÂGE, LA SANTÉ), table heads, column captions. Never smaller; tracking tightens to +0.06em in narrow columns. Table heads never wrap.

body.purpose: Interface text, player and table names, descriptions.

row-label.purpose: Stat-row labels at 12px: the typewriter is wide.

button.purpose: Buttons and tabs, typewriter bold, sentence case.

numeral.purpose: Every computed value on a row (Facultés, combat): one size per role.

numeral-total.purpose: Group totals and the XP left.

note.purpose: The notes, on 30px lines, 75 characters per line at most.

note-heading.purpose: Note headings, on the 30px line; smaller headings keep the text size, underlined with the pen.

shadows.name: feuille
shadows.purpose: The sheet on the table. None on phone, where the sheet fills the screen.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs, which also carry a double printed frame.

shadows.name: billet
shadows.purpose: Toasts, slips of paper pushed onto the sheet.

shadows.name: bougie-glow
shadows.purpose: Night only: amber glow in soft-light, fixed overlay at z-index 1250 below modals. Lights in 700ms, then holds still.

shadows.name: bougie-shade
shadows.purpose: Night only: brown shadow at the edges, under 12% until 80% of the radius; removed under prefers-contrast: more.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Arrivals: pages, ink dots, planet phase, stamp, slips, dialogs, points bar, second frame.

motion.name: ease-pen
motion.purpose: The pen stroke: steady, slowing only at the end of the word.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, preview colour arriving, pencil mark on an editable value.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons and stepper cells sink by 1px like a stamp; no Material ripple.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Turning page: a tab opens from the side of the tab chosen (16px and a fade); the first tab shown settles with a fade and a 6px rise.

motion.name: write
motion.purpose: Signature: a written or changed value traces itself left to right (clip-path, the Written atom); the strike over a saved value and the XP fill are drawn at the same pace.

motion.name: dry
motion.purpose: A validated preview fades back to ink.

motion.name: planet-phase
motion.purpose: The watercolour phase glides to its new value.

motion.name: ink-dot
motion.purpose: A gained Existence point lands like an ink drop, growing from its centre.

motion.name: blow
motion.value: 560ms ease-out; at 0 a second ripple, 760ms after 140ms
motion.purpose: A point lost on an Existence sends one ink ripple out of its planet, in its watercolour. Under reduced motion it lights up and goes out in place.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: "Validée" comes down slightly large and tilted, then settles: at validation and each validated purchase.

motion.name: billet
motion.purpose: A toast is pushed onto the sheet, tilted −1.5°, then straightens.

motion.name: pose
motion.purpose: A dialog is laid on the sheet, dropping 10px with a 0.6° tilt that straightens.

motion.name: points-bar
motion.purpose: Slides up from the bottom, keeping its last content while it leaves; the phone's Existences band slides down the same way. Fades under reduced motion.

motion.name: theme-crossfade
motion.purpose: Jour ↔ bougie crossfades the whole page (View Transitions).

motion.name: candle
motion.purpose: The night glow lights once and holds still: nothing loops on a sheet at rest.

motion.name: wash-bloom
motion.purpose: The plate's wash blooms in on arrival (the only movement on load); crossing Devenir 100 detaches the second frame (outline offset 0 → 4px).

motion.name: chevron
motion.purpose: Section collapse chevron rotation.

motion.name: collapse
motion.purpose: Section content collapse; the state is saved on the account.

motion.name: point-repeat
motion.purpose: Held − or + on a characteristic stepper; Shift+click steps 5.

breakpoints.name: existences-row
breakpoints.purpose: All four planets on one row; below it Maï drops under a rule, "seuil N" takes its own line, and on touch screens characteristic groups go one per row.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Below it: the sheet fills the screen, the Existences box scrolls and a 44px band takes over, tables become blocks, tabs scroll without arrows.

breakpoints.name: groups-three
breakpoints.purpose: Three characteristic groups and faculty columns side by side; two below.

breakpoints.name: plate-one-line
breakpoints.purpose: Portrait, name and facts on one line; below it Âge, Aspect and Devenir go under the name.

breakpoints.name: md

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Planet steppers inline after the value; skills on three columns; doodle in the plate.

breakpoints.name: three-columns
breakpoints.purpose: Caractères, Facultés and Combat on one screen (1.2fr / 1fr / 210px).

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The sheet widens from 1400px to 1680px so the inventory tables fit.

breakpoints.name: touch

narrative.overview:
The world is **Le carnet d'Oniria**. Every page is a character sheet printed on cream paper and filled in by hand, the way a sheet lives on the table across many evenings. A double printed frame runs around the page, and a title band carries a frieze of moon phases between two fleurons. The paper has its own grain, faint blue guide lines and a red margin. Over it sit pale atlas geometries (planets on their orbit, armillary spheres, constellations), soft watercolour washes and a few pen doodles. Oniria is a multiverse of moons (medieval, alien, steampunk worlds…), so the sheet belongs to no single genre: it speaks of moons, travel between worlds, and a story written game after game.

The system rests on one rule of writing. What the player writes is handwritten in blue ink (Caveat): the name, age, Aspect, Devenir, current Existences, characteristics, traits, items, notes. What the rules print or compute is typed (Courier Prime), with page and section titles stamped (Special Elite): labels, totals, maximums, thresholds, Facultés, combat values. Reading the sheet tells you at a glance what is yours and what the game derives.

There are two lights for the same paper. **Jour** is a sheet on a pale table. **Nuit** is the same sheet lit by a candle: warmer, muted paper, an amber glow from the top left, and brown shadow at the edges only, so the reading area keeps its contrast. Density is a per-account preference (Confort / Compact), and the layout keeps everything used in play visible without scrolling at 1440px and wider.

Motion has one signature: **writing**. A value the player writes, or that changes (a saved field, a −/+ on an Existence, a point added), traces itself left to right like a pen stroke (420ms, steady `cubic-bezier(0.45, 0.05, 0.35, 1)`). A validated preview dries: its colour fades back to ink over 600ms. Everything else is quiet continuity or feedback, played once, never on load:
- **Turning page:** a tab opens like a page of the notebook, sliding in from the side of the tab chosen (16px and a fade, 220ms); the first tab shown settles with a short fade and rise.
- **The blow:** a point lost on an Existence sends one ink ripple out of its planet, in the Existence's watercolour (560ms); at 0 a second, slower ripple follows. It only answers a loss, never the threshold, whose role the rules in this repository do not state.
- **The stamp:** "Validée" comes down like a rubber stamp, slightly large and tilted, then settles (300ms), when the sheet is validated and at each validated purchase.
- **Ink filling:** XP received fills the remaining part of its bar from left to right at the pen's pace (420ms).
- **Slips and cards:**
  - a toast arrives as a slip of paper pushed onto the sheet, tilted −1.5°, then straightens (280ms, leaves in 160ms);
  - a dialog is laid on the sheet, dropping 10px with a 0.6° tilt that straightens (260ms, leaves in 160ms).
- **Bars and light:**
  - the points bar slides up from the bottom (280ms) and leaves faster (160ms); the phone's Existences band slides down the same way;
  - the candle lights in 700ms, then holds still: a flame that flickers in a loop would recomposite the whole page on every frame for as long as the sheet stays open beside Discord;
  - Jour ↔ bougie crossfades the whole page (View Transitions, 450ms);
  - buttons press like a stamp (1px down), with no Material ripple.

Nothing moves on load except the plate's wash, which blooms in, and nothing loops on a sheet at rest: once a movement has played, the page stays still until something changes. Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, tracing, sliding, rising and tilting stop; fades and colour changes that carry state remain:
- pages, slips, dialogs, the stamp and the XP fill fade;
- the blow's ripple lights up and goes out in place, without growing.

The system rejects the clean "tool" look (identical boxed cards, a sterile interface type, stock Material colours) and anything that tires the eyes over a long evening.
keyCharacteristics: A printed sheet on paper: double frame, title band with moon phases, grain, guide lines and margin.
Handwritten blue ink for everything the player writes; typewriter for everything the rules print.
Existences as small atlas planets: printed orbit, watercolour phase, one pen-filled dot per point.
A personal moon tint per character, laid as a watercolour wash whose strength follows Devenir.
Two lights (Jour, bougie) on the same light paper, and two densities, chosen by the player.
One motion signature: values write themselves like a pen stroke, and previews dry into ink.

rules.name: The Plume Rule
rules.body: What the player writes is handwritten in blue ink; what the rules print or compute is typed in printing ink. A value never changes script when it changes state: an editable value is handwritten when read and when typed into.

rules.name: The Encre Bleue Rule
rules.body: Blue ink means "written by the player" or "you can act here". No other hue marks interaction, and nothing decorative is blue except pen doodles.

rules.name: The Couleur du Jeu Rule
rules.body: Existence colours appear only in the planets' watercolour, and moon tints only in a character's own identity (the plate wash, the portrait planet, the tint button). Neither becomes a UI accent.

rules.name: The Lune Personnelle Rule
rules.body: The plate's tint wash runs from 14% to 34% opacity as Devenir goes from 0 to 100. Above 100 (transcendance), the portrait gets a second frame in the tint, 4px outside the first. A missing Devenir sits at mid strength.

rules.name: The Aperçu Rule
rules.body: A value changed by pending points is a preview, not a fact: it turns semibold in succès (rising) or avertissement (falling), its saved value stays struck through before it, and "Avant : N" waits in a tooltip. Nothing returns to ink until the points are validated or cancelled.

rules.name: The Machine à écrire Rule
rules.body: Printed text is typewriter, never a system sans. Titles are stamped, never set in a display serif.

rules.name: The Pas d'italique Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from the three scripts, size and weight. Typed text has no italics; the hand carries its own slant. Courier Prime is served in roman only (400, 700), so no italic file is ever preloaded.

rules.name: The Papier Rule
rules.body: Nothing inside the sheet floats on a shadow. To lift something, lay raised paper on the sheet and give it a printed border.

rules.name: The Bougie Rule
rules.body: At night the candle is an overlay above the page and below modals (z-index 1250, no pointer events): an amber glow in soft-light at the top left, and a brown shadow that starts at 55% of the radius and stays under 12% opacity until 80%. Every ink keeps at least 4.5:1 where text sits. Under `prefers-contrast: more`, the candle is removed.

dos: **Do** write every value the player sets in Caveat, in blue ink, on a printed field line or row; type every computed value in Courier Prime.
**Do** stamp page and section titles in Special Elite, uppercase, with an armillary sphere and a running printed rule for sections.
**Do** frame printed areas (plate, Existences, portrait) as square boxes in printing ink; lay cards, menus and dialogs on the sheet as raised paper with a 1px border.
**Do** read colours through the theme's CSS variables (`var(--mui-palette-…)`, `theme.vars`, `color-mix()` for alpha); both themes are light paper, and the candle has its own inks.
**Do** keep every text ink at 4.5:1 or more on its paper, including near the candle's shadowed edges.
**Do** keep everything used in play visible without scrolling from 1440px; below that, keep Combat beside Caractères and Facultés.
**Do** keep doodles and constellations in blank areas, pale and `aria-hidden`, and never under a value.
**Do** show pending points as a preview across the whole sheet: semibold succès or avertissement, the saved value struck before, "Avant : N" in a tooltip.
**Do** keep loaded data on screen while it is re-read; show a spinner only when nothing has loaded yet.
**Do** honour both densities and both lights for every new surface.

**Do** animate a written value with the shared `.oniria-write` stroke (the `Written` atom), keep feedback under 300ms, and give every animation a reduced-motion path that keeps fades and colour changes.
donts: **Don't** use a system sans or a display serif: printed text is a typewriter, titles are a stamp, and the player's words are a hand.
**Don't** handwrite something the rules compute, or type something the player wrote.
**Don't** use blue ink for decoration, or any other hue for interaction.
**Don't** use Existence colours or moon tints outside the planets and the character's identity.
**Don't** add shadows inside the sheet; lift things with raised paper and a printed border.
**Don't** reintroduce a dark ground for the night: the candle warms and dims the same paper.
**Don't** add another −/+ style; steppers share one printed frame in two sizes.
**Don't** bind the sheet to one genre (parchment, chrome, neon): Oniria's moons are many worlds.
**Don't** add load choreography, scroll reveals, staggers or Material ripples; the sheet moves only when something is written, changes state or needs continuity.
